name: Tessera Suppression Lattice SL-3 'Quilt'
description:
A networked smart-weapon system consisting of four autonomous turrets that operate as a coordinated fire group. Each turret fires 5.56mm caseless rounds and is equipped with a sensor suite that shares target data across the network. The Suppression Lattice creates interlocking fields of fire that can deny access to an area up to 400 meters in diameter.

Tessera designed the SL-3 for corporate facility defense where manpower is expensive and perimeter coverage is critical. A single operator with a BCI link can manage a four-turret Lattice, designating priority targets and engagement zones while the turrets' AI handles tracking and fire control. The system can also operate autonomously using pre-programmed engagement protocols.

Each turret weighs 18 kg and can be deployed in under two minutes. The four-unit system uses encrypted mesh networking that maintains coordination even if individual turrets are destroyed or communication is jammed — the remaining units automatically redistribute their fire coverage to compensate for gaps.
legality: Corporate sovereign territory only — autonomous weapons restriction
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm caseless per turret
effective_range: 50-600 meters per turret
rate_of_fire: 600 rounds per minute per turret
capacity: 500 rounds per turret
weight: 18 kg per turret (72 kg total system)
power_source: Individual turret power cells, 48 hours standby / 20 minutes sustained fire
tactical_use: The Quilt is deployed as an area denial system that multiplies a small security force's coverage capability. A four-turret Lattice controlled by a single BCI-linked operator can secure a perimeter that would traditionally require a dozen personnel with conventional weapons. The AI fire control ensures efficient ammunition distribution — the system prioritizes threats and avoids wasting rounds on suppressed or neutralized targets. The turrets' cross-networked sensors make flanking or concealment extremely difficult within the Lattice's engagement zone.
cultural_context: The Suppression Lattice represents Tessera's vision of automated warfare — minimal human involvement, maximum coverage, algorithmic efficiency. Labor organizations have criticized the system as a tool for replacing human security workers with autonomous killing machines. Tessera's response is that the SL-3 protects human security personnel by reducing their exposure to danger. Both statements are true, and neither addresses the growing discomfort with AI-controlled weapons making lethal decisions.
story_hooks: A Suppression Lattice was deployed in a residential district after a corporate facility expanded its sovereign territory boundary. The turrets' engagement zone now covers a public thoroughfare, and three pedestrians have been killed for walking too close to the new perimeter.

Someone has hacked a Lattice's mesh network and reprogrammed it to protect a territory that Tessera does not own. The turrets are defending a squatter community, and Tessera cannot remotely shut them down.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular autonomous turret with a distinctly modular design. Low-profile polygonal body sits on a stabilized tripod base, topped with a rotating sensor head and barrel assembly. Appears engineered rather than organic — all hard geometry and purposeful mounting points.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 38 cm (turret body), 48 cm (with sensor head raised). Width: 32 cm (base footprint). Depth: 28 cm. Barrel length: 22 cm (5.56mm caseless).
physical_description.weight_description: Solid and deliberate — 18 kg feels substantial but portable. Balanced on the tripod with a low center of gravity. Designed to be man-portable but not light.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy chassis with steel reinforcement plates at stress points. Titanium barrel assembly. Sensor dome is hardened polycarbonate composite.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed aluminum accents. Polymer components are textured dark gray to reduce glint. Minimal reflective surfaces — designed for low visibility.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte gunmetal gray primary, with charcoal black mounting brackets and power conduits. Accent strips of deep blue along the sensor array (Tessera corporate branding). Red status indicator ring around the barrel collar.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip points on the tripod legs for deployment. Control surfaces are knurled steel. Mounting points have rubberized quick-release handles.
distinctive_features: Rotating sensor head with lidless optic clusters arranged in overlapping arcs
Integrated mesh-network antenna array (thin copper fins protruding from upper body)
Red/amber/green status indicator ring encircling the barrel mount
Tessera angular logo stamped into the base plate
Quick-release ammunition feed system with visible 500-round magazine loading port
Thermal venting grilles running along both flanks of the turret body
Articulated barrel assembly that allows independent elevation adjustment
Small blue LED port on the rear for BCI uplink synchronization
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera corporate logo (angular T-shape) prominently stamped on the base. Serial number plate on left flank. Tessera SL-3 designation and 'QUILT UNIT 1/4' printed on a small placard near the mounting interface.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show minor wear: dust accumulation on sensor domes, slight polymer scuffing on mounting legs, burn marks around the barrel collar from sustained fire. Well-maintained corporate systems appear pristine. Ungoverned/black-market units show improvised repairs and aftermarket modifications.
